_readme: Every number and the routing table for the overnight edit queue. Dan's decisions live here so one row can be flipped without touching code. Procedure: scripts/edit-queue/README.md.

routing._decided: Dan, 2026-09-17. A fixed rule, not an A/B test. No automatic re-routing: a change is Dan's call.

unattended._why: Phase 1 pilot: jobs with no AI-clip slots, small only. Widen in Phase 3, after Phase 2 builds the placeholder flow for raw cuts.

review._why: One editor owns the candidate, then one independent reviewer returns one consolidated verdict. Rejected candidates park for a separately scoped revision; there is no automatic supervisor/fix/re-review loop.

codex._proven: 2026-09-17. workspace-write passed a smoke test (work dir, project ffmpeg, queue.py, rclone once ~/.config/rclone was writable) but FAILED the first real job (DS-01): that sandbox denies /bin/ps, and every edit must run ps to respect the two-build cap. danger-full-access is what Dan's own ~/.codex/config.toml already uses for his daily Codex sessions, so a queue session has the same rights as a hand-fired one. approval_policy=never in both cases: nothing ever prompts.
codex._models: Dan, 2026-09-17: edits run Sol / high (Codex) and Opus / high (Claude). Commit 3403c6b overwrote this to Sol/medium + Fable/high by accident; restored 2026-09-18 by the Phase 0 proof session.

claude._proven: 2026-09-17 20:14 (AV-01, first real launch): the flags below start a session that works with no prompt (9 minutes of real cut-scanning in the work dir). It ended when the ACCOUNT's 5-hour usage window, shared with Dan's daytime sessions, was already spent ('You've hit your monthly spend limit ... your session limit resets 9pm'). The dispatcher cannot see remaining allowance before launching; the usage-limit back-off is the only guard, so its patterns must match that wording.

_usage_limit_patterns_why: 2026-09-17 AV-01 run: Claude's real wording was 'You've hit your monthly spend limit ... your session limit resets 9pm' and matched none of the first seven, so the run was filed session_failed/stalled instead of usage_limited/ready with the 2-hour back-off.
